# Nirodhavāra (Ya 5.2.2)

**ID:** Ya 5.2.2
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Nirodhavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m4.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2) is the second subsection of the *Pavattivāra* (process section) within the *Saccayamaka*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma *Yamaka* [Anderson 1999]. In this section, the text analyzes the condition of beings who are reborn or pass away in various realms with respect to the cessation (*nirodha*) of the four noble truths in relation to one another [Anderson 1999]. In standard *Yamaka* style, this inquiry is carried out using paired questions applied across different temporal divisions—the present, the past, the future, and combinations of these time frames [Anderson 1999; Nyanatiloka 2007].

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reflect the pervasive formulaic parallelism of the *Yamaka*, showing thousands of shared segments with closely related texts [DharmaNexus]. Internally, *Nirodhavāra* shares its largest blocks of material with its sibling chapters in the *Saccayamaka*—*Uppādavāra* (Ya 5.2.1) and *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.3)—as well as corresponding *Nirodhavāra* chapters elsewhere in the *Yamaka*, including the *Āyatanayamaka* (Ya 3.2.2), *Indriyayamaka* (Ya 9.2.2), and *Dhātuyamaka* (Ya 6.2.2) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects conceptual and formulaic correspondences with Tibetan translations of Indian scholastic treatises, notably the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4091) and the *Pañcaskandhabhāṣya* (D4068) [DharmaNexus].
